testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you check extra carefully before driving in winter?
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your coolant and antifreeze levels, heating and defrosting equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer, tires, tire chains, lights, reflectors, windows, mirrors, handholds, steps, radiator shutters, and exhaust system.

questions.question: Strong winds cause the most problems for which type of vehicle?
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard for drivers to control their vehicles. Lighter vehicles are affected more by strong winds than heavier ones.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, what should you do?

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Pull in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain control.

questions.question: How should you prevent cargo from sliding?
questions.explanation: Cargo that slides makes steering and handling difficult. Use blocking in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo to keep it from moving.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Checking critical items only at the beginning and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking critical items only at the beginning and end of a trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during your trip, not just at the start and end. Check the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to catch problems early.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning happen most often?

options.text: A vehicle is traveling faster than 60 mph.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens most often on wet roads when tire pressure is too low and tire tread is too worn. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What should you do when asked to make a lane change during the driving test?

options.text: You should not be concerned with other motorists.
You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
You should make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if that means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: When making a lane change, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of when to upshift?
questions.explanation: Upshift based on engine speed (RPM) and road speed (MPH). Read your manual to learn the RPM range and watch your speedometer. Time is not an indicator for shifting.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air, what does this mean?

options.text: You should not be concerned as this is a normal process.
There is something wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is something wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only to prevent pressure from getting too high. If it releases air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic fix it.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop and sleep if you feel tired while driving. Do not try to push on to your destination. Coffee cannot replace sleep.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not be more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, air brakes should lose no more than 2 psi in one minute. If the air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
Complete it as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always follow the same steps in the same order.
questions.explanation: Perform pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important steps and prevents you from missing anything.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Explosives are classified as Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo:

options.text: Can be safer than properly loaded cargo.

questions.explanation: Cargo that is not properly loaded or secured is dangerous to the driver and to others on the road.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure a 10-foot piece of cargo?
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, always use at least two tie-downs, regardless of cargo size.

questions.question: When asked to make a turn during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Not use a turn signal since you were told to turn.
Check traffic only to your right.

questions.explanation: When making a turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill, make a decision quickly because:

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will move out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: Make your decision quickly when brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle moves, and the harder it becomes to stop.

questions.question: To avoid slowing down traffic in a large truck, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: When approaching your vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, you should look under it to:

options.text: See if the vehicle is on an incline.
Check for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel.
See if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting your vehicle, check its general condition and look for damage or leaning. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Also check around the vehicle for hazards that could block movement, such as people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo hitting them.
Protect the driver's head when getting into the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo hitting them.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver from cargo that moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: Windshield wiper blades should be:
questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage and make sure they are firmly attached to the vehicle.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Complete a full vehicle inspection to check if the vehicle is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete a full vehicle inspection to check if the vehicle is safe.
questions.explanation: To get a CDL, you must pass a vehicle inspection test. An examiner will watch you inspect a vehicle.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Steer with one hand and keep the other hand free.

questions.explanation: Follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if conditions are bad. Slow down even more if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Can damage parts of a vehicle.
Is needed to warm up parts of a vehicle.
Helps improve a vehicle's gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage parts of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually so your vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can harm the engine and other parts.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact so you can communicate with them.
Stay in their path of travel.

questions.explanation: Get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as it may make them more aggressive. Do not react to their actions.

questions.question: When a vehicle starts, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After an engine starts, the coolant temperature should rise gradually to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes to slow down. This makes your brake lights flash and warns drivers behind you.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.explanation: Check that dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, you should inspect it:

options.text: Only at the start of a trip.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.explanation: Check cargo and its securing devices before starting a trip. During the trip, check them within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: Are probably aware of the roadway.
May be focused on the repair and not paying attention to traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not paying attention to traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people fixing a disabled vehicle on the side of the road. They may be concentrating on the repair and not watching for traffic.

questions.question: How many driver's licenses can a person have?

options.text: Two licenses: one for cars and one for trucks.
One license for each state where they drive.

questions.explanation: You can have only one license. Having more than one is illegal. You can be punished with jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.

questions.question: How can you avoid distracted driving?

options.text: Eat while driving to stay alert.
Avoid having complex conversations with passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid having complex conversations with passengers.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for objects), mental (talking with passengers), or both (texting). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you leave, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: What should you do if your brakes fail while driving downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Let rumble strips slow your vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill, find an escape ramp to stop your vehicle. If there is no escape ramp, use the safest option available, such as driving into an open field or side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Only if you think something is wrong.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic around you and notice any problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do shortly after changing a tire?

options.text: Stop and check that the lug nuts are tight.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop a short time later and check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: How should you apply the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly and steadily when stopping. Gradual braking helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, what should your vehicle do?
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting objects or vehicles behind you.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Your position may change, so your mirrors may need adjustment each time.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. If you see rust in this area, check that the nuts are tight.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should the weight be placed?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Weight placed high makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible to keep your vehicle stable and safe.

questions.question: When loading cargo, it is important to:

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
Know the weight capacity of your vehicle's suspension system.
Place light items underneath heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the weight capacity of your vehicle's suspension system.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make sure their vehicle is not overloaded. You need to know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can safely carry, including the suspension system's weight limit.

questions.question: If you are unsure if your vehicle can safely pass under a bridge, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are unsure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down as you approach it. If possible, find an alternate route.

questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as fire extinguishers, is:

options.text: Only needed in vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Required in all commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required in all commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must carry the proper emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no more than three feet high.
Should be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: All cargo in a trailer must be properly secured so it does not shift or move while the vehicle is in transit.

questions.question: One way to avoid aggressive driving is to:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Set realistic expectations about how long your trip will take.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set realistic expectations about how long your trip will take.
questions.explanation: To prevent frustration that can lead to aggressive driving, plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include driving at a safe speed, keeping a safe distance from other vehicles, not making angry gestures, and keeping both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use only one set of turn signals.

questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: A second conviction for operating a commercial vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher will result in:

options.text: The loss of your CDL for life.
The loss of your CDL for five years.
The loss of your CDL for one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: The loss of your CDL for life.
questions.explanation: Operating a commercial vehicle with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal. A first offense costs you your CDL for one year. A second offense costs you your CDL for life.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Always pump the brakes several times before holding down the brake pedal.
Press down the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you slow or stop.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in vehicles with ABS as you would in vehicles without ABS. When ABS works properly, it automatically activates when braking in situations that could cause the wheels to lock.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press down the brake pedal quickly.
Press down the brake pedal gradually.
Lift up the brake pedal quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press down the brake pedal gradually.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal down smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system has very low pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system has too little pressure. If air pressure gets too low while driving, exit the road and park as soon as possible.
